title: CMM-Math: A Chinese Multimodal Math Dataset To Evaluate and Enhance the Mathematics Reasoning of Large Multimodal Models
extended_summary:
This paper does not report a ChatGPT-based mathematics intervention study in grades 6–8. Instead, it introduces CMM-Math, a large Chinese multimodal mathematics benchmark and training dataset designed to evaluate and improve the mathematical reasoning of large multimodal models (LMMs). The dataset contains over 28,000 problems spanning 12 grade levels from elementary school through high school, with multiple problem types, images, and detailed solutions.

The authors also propose Math-LMM, a multimodal model trained in three stages: foundational pre-training, foundational fine-tuning, and mathematical fine-tuning. The model is evaluated against several open-source and closed-source LMMs, including GPT-4o, Gemini, Qwen-VL, and others, using accuracy and GPT-4o-based scoring on CMM-Math and on external benchmarks (MATHVISTA and MATH-V). The paper reports that the task is challenging for current models, especially on harder levels and geometry-related topics, and that Math-LMM improves performance relative to some open-source baselines.

For the retrieval query, the closest comparator evidence is benchmark/model-evaluation work rather than an educational intervention. The paper includes mathematics problems from grades corresponding to elementary, middle school, and high school, but it does not study student learning outcomes, classroom implementation, or any counterfactual comparison involving ChatGPT in grades 6–8.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed benchmark/modeling paper with extensive quantitative evaluation, but it is not an educational intervention study and does not use a student-level experimental design. The evidence is methodologically clear for model benchmarking, but relevance to K-12 learning impact is indirect.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper shows moderate-to-large differences in benchmark accuracy among models, but these are not student outcome effects and do not demonstrate classroom learning impact. Its practical significance is mainly for model development and assessment infrastructure rather than direct educational improvement.

interventions.use_case: Chinese multimodal math benchmark/dataset construction and evaluation of large multimodal models for solving grade 1-12 mathematics problems with images and text; also includes training a custom Math-LMM on the dataset.
Evaluating and fine-tuning general-purpose multimodal foundation models such as GPT-4o, Gemini, Qwen-VL, and open-source LMMs on mathematical reasoning tasks.

finding.finding_summary: This paper does not study student learning in classrooms; it benchmarks model performance on multimodal mathematics problems across 12 grade levels. On CMM-Math, mean accuracy across models was 35.66, with GPT-4o (3-shot) reaching 65.98 and Math-LMM (72B) reaching 48.57, while many open models performed much lower. Performance declined substantially on harder grades and geometry-heavy subjects, indicating the dataset is challenging for current models.
finding.measure: Accuracy on CMM-Math multimodal math benchmark; GPT-4o scored model outputs on fill-in-the-blank and analysis items
finding.study_size: n=28,069 problems (evaluation subset n=5,821; training subset n=22,248)

finding.finding_summary: The proposed Math-LMM improved benchmark performance relative to several open-source multimodal baselines. Math-LMM (72B) achieved 48.57 overall accuracy on CMM-Math and 36.3 on MathVista, outperforming the smaller 7B version (32.10 on CMM-Math; 34.9 on MathVista) and many open-source comparators, though it still lagged behind some closed-source models on certain metrics.
finding.measure: Accuracy/GPT-4o score on CMM-Math, MathVista, and MATH-V
finding.study_size: n=28,069 CMM-Math problems; secondary benchmarks MathVista testmini and MATH-V test set
